To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated the first electroluminescence from a single-layer device containing an amphiphilic metal chelate complex as an emitting material, bis(N-hexadeclyl-8-hydroxquinoline) cadmium (Cd(Hq)2), with a low driving voltage of 7 V.

we have developed a new type of EL material, a bisquinoline metal complex, that exhibits high EL efficiency, high stability, and low driving voltage, which are all important characteristics for commercialization.

we have found a new material for electroluminescence, bis[N-hydroxy-8-hydro-2-quinolonecarboxamide]cadium, which emits light in greenish-yellow color, and that we have made electroluminescense devices with this material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of EL material.
the design, synthesis, and characterization of new amphiphilic complexes for application in EL devices.
the synthesis of new amphiphilic materials and the construction of EL devices using them as the emitter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the EL emission from the single layer device is attributed to the emission of the Cd(HQ)2 molecules, and the EL mechanism is a recombination of injected electrons and holes at the emitting molecules in the bulk.
the present EL device using the Cd(HQ)2 complex is one of the best EL devices reported to date.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have succeeded in the development of a novel EL device with a single emitting layer using a highly fluorescent complex as the emitter material.
the use of a single layer structure is effective in the fabrication of a highly efficient EL device using Cd(HQ)2.
the use of a single-layer structure and a fluorescent emitter material with a high quantum yield is a promising approach to fabricating high efficiency EL devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the EL emission of the Cd(HQ)2 complex is not quenched by the Al cathode, in contrast to the case of other fluorescent complexes, such as tris(8-hydroxyquinolinolato) aluminum (Alq3) and tris(4-methoxy-8-hydroquinolinolato)-aluminum(III) (MeOAlq3).
Cd(HQ)2 is a promising candidate for the fabrication of low-cost, high-efficiency EL devices.
this material has the potential to be a good emitter for use in organic electroluminescence devices.
